bottleneck: The agent routes toward an uncarried parcel through a door without first collecting the co-located key, so the door blocks 3 consecutive moves in key-door-delivery.
rationale: Evidence shows the key-door-delivery run made 3 blocked 'move right' actions ('A key is required to cross this door') while a key was co-located with the agent at (0,0) and the target parcel at (1,0) sat behind a door at (1,0). Prioritizing collection of the co-located key (an access resource) before routing through the gate satisfies the prerequisite and unblocks delivery. The extension defers (returns undefined) whenever no door is present, no non-co-located pending parcel exists, or no co-located key is available, preserving holdout behavior in simple-delivery, two-parcels, detour-delivery, and battery-return (all have zero doors).
expectedMetric: Blocked transitions in key-door-delivery reduced from 3 to 0 and delivery achieved (score 10 vs 0).
